title: AuditVerifyResult
description: Response payload from `GET /audit/verify` per spec/v1/auth-profiles.md §`openwop-audit-log-integrity` §4 'Verification endpoint'. Hosts advertising the audit-log-integrity profile MUST return this shape on the verify endpoint when called with a valid `audit:read`-scoped credential. The shape carries the verifier's chain-validity verdict, the in-range signed checkpoints, and any anomaly records the verifier detected while re-walking the hash chain.

fromSeq.description: Echo of the caller's `fromSeq` query parameter. The verifier MUST re-walk entries [fromSeq, toSeq] inclusive.

toSeq.description: Echo of the caller's `toSeq` query parameter. MUST be >= fromSeq.

chainValid.description: True when every entry's `prevHash` matches the SHA-256 of the prior entry's RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization AND every signed checkpoint in `checkpoints[]` verifies against the host's advertised `auditLogIntegrity.checkpointPublicKey`. False when ANY anomaly is detected: a chain break, a mutated or missing entry, a checkpoint root that does not recompute, or an invalid signature. `anomalies[]` enumerates them (RFC 0218 §C).

checkpointsValid.description: OPTIONAL companion bit: true when every checkpoint signature in `checkpoints[]` verifies. Distinguishes 'chain broken but checkpoints OK' from 'checkpoints forged but chain intact'. Hosts MAY omit when `chainValid` already conveys the verdict; clients that distinguish the two failure modes SHOULD prefer hosts that surface this bit explicitly.

checkpoints.description: Signed checkpoints emitted within [fromSeq, toSeq]. Order: ascending by `atSequence`. Empty array MUST appear when no checkpoint was emitted in the window (not omitted).

anomalies.description: One entry per anomaly detected in [fromSeq, toSeq]: a chain break, a mutated or missing entry, or a checkpoint whose root or signature fails (RFC 0218 §C). Empty array MUST appear when chainValid is true (not omitted), and MUST be non-empty when chainValid is false.

checkpoint.description: Host-issued checkpoint id. Globally unique within the host's audit log.

atSequence.description: Audit-log sequence number at which the checkpoint was minted. Inclusive — the entry at this sequence is covered by the checkpoint's merkleRoot.

merkleRoot.description: Lowercase-hex Merkle root over the entries this checkpoint anchors: sequence in (P, atSequence], P the previous checkpoint's atSequence or 0. Leaves are the entries' hashes (SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS) in sequence order; a parent is SHA-256 of the ASCII bytes left ‖ right; a last odd node is promoted unchanged (auth-profiles.md §Audit-log integrity 3, RFC 0218). Verifiers re-compute and compare, holding the leaf count to atSequence − P; a mismatch implies chain mutation since the previous checkpoint.

signature.description: Base64-encoded Ed25519 signature over the 32 bytes `merkleRoot` hex-decodes to (not its hex text, not the checkpoint object), verifiable with the host's advertised `auditLogIntegrity.checkpointPublicKey` (RFC 0218).

Anomaly.description: One detected anomaly (RFC 0218 §C). `kind` says what failed and fixes which members the entry carries: `chain-break` carries `expectedPrevHash` and `actualPrevHash`; `merkle-mismatch` and `signature-invalid` carry `checkpoint`; `hash-mismatch` and `missing-entry` carry neither. An entry without `kind` is a `chain-break`, the only shape this object had before RFC 0218 §C. A verifier MUST treat an unknown `kind` as an anomaly: `chainValid` is false whenever `anomalies` is non-empty.

atSeq.description: The sequence number the anomaly is at. For an entry kind, the entry that failed (`chain-break`, `hash-mismatch`) or the first missing sequence of a gap (`missing-entry`). For a checkpoint kind, the checkpoint's `atSequence`.

kind.description: What failed. `chain-break`: the entry's `prevHash` is not the hash of the entry before it. `hash-mismatch`: the entry no longer hashes to the value the host recorded when it was appended (the entry was mutated in place). `missing-entry`: no entry exists at `atSeq` inside the verified range. `merkle-mismatch`: the root recomputed over the checkpoint's range (RFC 0218 §A) differs from its `merkleRoot`. `signature-invalid`: the checkpoint's `signature` does not verify under the advertised `checkpointPublicKey`. Hosts SHOULD set it; absent means `chain-break`.

expectedPrevHash.description: `chain-break` only. Hex-encoded SHA-256 the verifier computed from the prior entry's RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization; `null` when the entry is the genesis entry, whose `prevHash` must be null.

actualPrevHash.description: `chain-break` only. The `prevHash` value the audit-log entry actually carries, `null` included. Empty string when the field is missing (a structural anomaly distinct from a hash mismatch).

checkpoint.description: `merkle-mismatch` and `signature-invalid` only: the id of the failing checkpoint, as in `checkpoints[].checkpoint`. Required because two checkpoints can share an `atSequence` while a rotating key dual-signs (auth-profiles.md §Key management).

detail.description: OPTIONAL human-readable explanation for an operator. Not machine-readable; a verifier MUST NOT branch on it.
